properties.project_name: Mission Creek Park -- east reach (Pavilion to 4th St bridge)
properties.digitized_from: Hand-traced from satellite imagery (contextily/Esri World Imagery), guided step-by-step by the owner (who knows this stretch directly) rather than the PDF-pixel transform, which repeatedly mis-located this segment.
properties.digitization_method: ADDED 2026-09-19: fills the gap between the already-tracked Mission Creek Park (which stops at its own NE corner near 235 Berry St/the 4th St bridge) and the already-tracked Mission Creek Park Pavilion further east -- OCII's plan labels P1 and P3 both fall in this stretch (per the neighboring records' own p_number notes, sourced from OCII's Nov 2024 CAC 'Remaining Mission Bay Open Space Parcels Update'; which built segment is P1 vs P3 is not resolved by that source and is not resolved here either). The owner corrected three successive attempts at locating and sizing this by satellite-derived pixel transform alone (which is exactly the failure mode this project's own header notes already warn about) before switching to owner-guided tracing: first a wrong area entirely (a bad 2-point transform), then a too-narrow shoreline-path-only trace, then a too-wide trace that ate into the paved road on the south side. Final shape: the full visible landscaped extent from the Pavilion to the 4th St bridge, at the width the owner confirmed, trimmed to exclude the Pavilion's own already-tracked footprint (400 sqm overlap removed). Checked against src/street_geometry.py's real street buffer: 0% clipped -- this stretch corresponds to a 'paper' (platted but never built) segment of Channel St, per src/street_geometry.py's own NOT_YET_REAL_CENTERLINE_LAYERS filter, consistent with it being built out as park instead of road. 2026-09-29 accuracy audit: correction to the P1/P3 statement above: on page 2 of the cited OCII Nov 2024 deck, the 'MISSION CREEK PARK P1' label points at the south-bank strip up to the 4th St bridge and 'MISSION CREEK PARK P3' at the wider green east of 4th St toward 3rd St/China Basin, so the source does resolve it: the traced stretch (Pavilion to the 4th St bridge, south bank) is P1, and P3 lies outside it. p_number and notes were corrected to say so; the file name and record id keep 'p1_p3' for now (a rename is left for the owner). project_name's extent wording ('east reach (Pavilion to 4th St bridge)') is our own description of the trace, not from a source. OCII's open-space page lists 'P1 Amphitheater at Mission Creek Park' and 'P3 Mission Creek Park' and is now cited.
properties.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- hand-traced from satellite imagery with the owner's direct, iterative guidance (not a surveyed footprint or GIS file from the project team, and not derived from the PDF-pixel transform, which was unreliable for this specific stretch). Status 'complete' because landscaping (paths, trees and grass) is visible on the strip in USDA NAIP imagery (viewed 2026-09-29) and in the earlier Esri imagery; the cited OCII deck shows 'Mission Creek Park (P3)' as a photo slide with no status text, and no cited source dates or confirms completion of P1.
properties.notes: OCII plan label P1 (see p_number); an earlier version of this note said the record covers P1 and P3 combined, which the Nov 2024 map does not support. OCII's open-space page lists 'P1 Amphitheater at Mission Creek Park' and 'P3 Mission Creek Park'.
properties.p_number: P1, per page 2 of OCII's Nov 2024 CAC update ('Remaining Mission Bay Open Space Parcels Update'), whose 'MISSION CREEK PARK P1' label points at this south-bank stretch up to the 4th St bridge; its 'MISSION CREEK PARK P3' label is on the wider green east of 4th St, outside this trace. (Earlier text said P1 and P3, unresolved; that was not what the source shows.)
